key_insight: A high-throughput computational search identified 58 candidate CuI-based ternary p-type transparent conductors, expanding design rules beyond oxide materials and linear Cu coordination.
engineering_relevance: These materials could expand transparent hole-conducting options for transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics, although solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Search X–Cu–I crystal structures using minima hopping and density functional theory.
Filter candidates for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
Analyze Cu coordination, valence-band dispersion, and stoichiometric origins of intrinsic holes.
evidence_signal: The calculations identified 49 previously unreported candidates and 20 p-type degenerate semiconductors, including Cu₂FI₂ with a calculated 3.75 eV gap and hole effective mass of 0.262 m₀.
watch_item: Computational predictions require experimental validation of synthesis, transparency, and conductivity before photovoltaic integration.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
